Each colour class must have at least 4 squares, and 16 colours are achievable.

**Upper bound.** Take any square S of some colour. It has at least two same-coloured neighbours. Consider the graph on one colour's squares, with edges between adjacent squares. Every vertex has degree at least 2, so the graph contains a cycle. A cycle in the grid graph must have even length and cannot have length 2, so it has at least 4 squares. Hence each colour covers at least 4 squares, and the number of colours is at most 64/4 = 16.

**Construction.** Split the board into sixteen 2×2 blocks and give each block its own colour. Every square then has exactly two same-coloured neighbours, one horizontally and one vertically. This uses 16 colours.

ANSWER: 16
